name: Herzog Johann von Brabant
credit: Herzog Johann von Brabant, miniature in the Codex Manesse (Heidelberg, Cod. Pal. germ. 848), c. 1300–1340 · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: John I, duke of Brabant and victor of the battle of Worringen in 1288, was a prince who also wrote songs, preserved in the Codex Manesse.
One of his songs appears here in Frank C. Nicholson’s translation, Old German Love Songs (1907), made from the minnesingers of the twelfth to fourteenth centuries.

poems.title: At Early Morning
poems.author: Herzog Johann von Brabant
poems.text:
At early morning I arose
On a day in May,
And to a pleasant orchard-close
I would go to play.
There I found three maidens gay;
One by one they sang this glee:
Harbalorifee, harbalorifee, harbalorifee!

When I saw the plants that sprang
In the orchard there,
And hearkened to the songs they sang,
Those three maidens fair,
My heart grew blithe and free from care,
And I, too, must sing this glee:
Harbalorifee, harbalorifee, harbalorifee!

Then to one I made salute,
The loveliest to view!
Round her waist my arm I put
Without more ado.
Fain I would have kissed her too.
Quoth she then, "Let be, let be!"
Harbalorifee, harbalorifee, harbalorifee!
